title: Single-slit diffraction; Reflection and refraction
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W08-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-1#N.6a, W08-1#N.7c, W04-1#N.9a, W08-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Wavefront
items.clue: Line or surface joining points that are in phase, such as every crest.

items.label: Diffraction
items.clue: Spreading out of a wave as it passes through a gap or around the edge of an obstacle.

items.label: Refraction
items.clue: Change in direction as a transmitted wave changes speed on crossing a boundary at an angle.

items.label: Normal
items.clue: Line at 90° to a surface at the point where light meets it; every angle is measured from it.

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: Predict first. Monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm is incident normally on a single slit, and the diffraction pattern is viewed on a distant screen. The slit width is then reduced from 0.20 mm to 0.10 mm. How does the central maximum change?

options.text: It becomes half as wide and less intense, as it is an image of a slit that is now half as wide.
It is unchanged, as both slits are far wider than 600 nm, so neither diffracts significantly.
It becomes twice as wide and less intense, as less light passes and is spread over a wider angle.
It becomes twice as wide, with unchanged peak intensity, which depends only on the source.

questions.stem: A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?

Sea waves reach a harbour wall with a 20 m wide entrance. A boat is moored behind the wall, well to one side of the entrance. On day 1 the waves have a wavelength of 20 m; on day 2, 2.0 m, with the same amplitude. On which day is the boat rocked more, and why?

options.text: Day 1: the wavelength is about the width of the gap, so the waves spread widely.
Day 2: shorter waves have a higher frequency, so they carry more energy around the wall.
Neither: the gap is the same width both days, and the gap alone sets the spreading.
Day 2: shorter waves fit through the gap more easily, so more of them pass behind it.
